name: Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills
venue: arXiv:2603.25158 (cs.AI). Submitted 26 Mar 2026 (v1), last revised 4 Jun 2026 (v5). Preprint marked 'Work in Progress'; no peer-reviewed venue listed as of the cited version. (Note: the survey-task title 'Consolidating Trajectories into a Durable Skill Directory' is a paraphrase; the actual arXiv title is 'Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills'.)
authors_affiliation: Jingwei Ni (lead/core contributor; ETH Zurich and University of Zurich), Yihao Liu (core; Peking University), Xinpeng Liu (core; Peking University), Yutao Sun (core; Zhejiang University) [these four marked as core contributors / equal contribution], Mengyu Zhou (corresponding author; zhoumengyu.zmy@alibaba-inc.com), Pengyu Cheng, Dexin Wang, Erchao Zhao, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang. Primary affiliation: Qwen Large Model Application Team, Alibaba; academic collaborators at ETH Zurich / University of Zurich, Peking University, and Zhejiang University.
code_url: https://github.com/Qwen-Applications/Trace2Skill (Apache-2.0; official codebase; releases the top spreadsheet skills and the spreadsheet evolution pipeline; ~107 stars at time of access)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Qwen-Applications/Trace2Skill (releases evolved xlsx skills under released_skills/: trace2skill-xlsx-35B-combined, xlsx-35B, trace2skill-xlsx-122B-combined, xlsx-122B; no leaderboard/paper-list maintained)
task_domain: LLM-agent tool-use / file-and-office workflows (spreadsheet/xlsx editing on SpreadsheetBench, plus PDF, DOCX, PPTX document agents), math reasoning (DAPO, AIME), and vision/document QA (DocVQA). Core focus is agentic file-manipulation 'skill' creation and deepening, with table-QA (WikiTableQuestions, HiTab) as OOD transfer.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent skill evolution with binary correctness supervision on an evolving set, but no gradient updates. A fixed (frozen-weight) LLM agent pi_theta runs a ReAct-style harness (with bash + Python file tools) using an initial skill S0 over a disjoint evolving set D_evolve to collect labeled success/failure trajectories; an offline pipeline then turns these traces into an improved skill S* = E(S0, D_evolve; pi_theta) such that pass rate on a held-out D_test improves, WITHOUT updating model parameters theta and WITHOUT any test-time retrieval. Two regimes: Skill Deepening (start from a human-written skill, e.g. Anthropic's official xlsx skill) and Skill Creation (start from a weak LLM-generated parametric draft, or No Skill for math/VQA). 100% self-evolution: the same model is trajectory generator, analyst, and merge operator (no external teacher). The setting is single-agent at deployment, but uses many parallel analyst sub-agents during the offline evolution stage (128 sub-agents in parallel in the main spreadsheet runs).
what_is_retrieved: Nothing is retrieved at test time. Trace2Skill is explicitly retrieval-free at inference: the consolidated skill (a SKILL.md directory + references/) is loaded unchanged. During the OFFLINE evolution stage, the system consolidates execution trajectories (successes and failures) into trajectory-level skill patches / distilled lessons that are merged into one skill. So the 'consumed' items are agent execution traces (and the lessons / SoPs distilled from them); the produced/used artifact is a static skill document, not retrieved memory items.
retrieval_grounding: Offline-induced GROWING-into-STATIC: the source of evidence is a growing pool of the agent's own episodic trajectories (self-written experience), but Trace2Skill compresses them once, offline, into a STATIC skill directory used at inference with no retrieval. There is no static external corpus/KB/API and no live test-time memory store. (Its compared baseline ReasoningBank instead keeps a growing retrievable memory queried at test time; Trace2Skill deliberately avoids that.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a top-k ranking objective. The objective is to consolidate the COMPLETE pool of trajectory-level patches into one coherent skill (default '+Combined' / full aggregation applies all consolidated patches), preferring prevalent recurring patterns and discarding idiosyncratic ones. The paper shows patch value is COMBINATORIAL (greedy top-1 selection plateaus below full aggregation; side-effects flip previously-correct tasks), motivating holistic consolidation over greedy/precision-driven subset selection. An optional Bayesian-optimization patch-subset selector is studied but is not the default.
retrieval_unit: Offline unit consumed: a full execution trajectory tau_i (query + reasoning/tool-use history + final output + binary correctness). Offline unit produced: a trajectory-level skill patch (a diff-style edit proposing additions to SKILL.md / references), and after merging, a guideline-rule / Standard-Operating-Procedure (SoP) section in a skill directory. At inference the 'unit' loaded is the whole skill document (SKILL.md + auxiliary references), not a retrieved snippet.
index_source: Offline-induced static store. The skill is built once from evolving-set trajectories (Stage 1 trajectory generation -> Stage 2 parallel patch proposal -> Stage 3 hierarchical consolidation) and then frozen; it does NOT grow at test time. Trajectory corpus is itself growing/episodic during collection but the final retrievable/usable artifact is a fixed skill directory.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical human-readable skill DIRECTORY: a root SKILL.md holding broadly-applicable procedural SoPs, plus a references/ folder of on-demand auxiliary files/scripts/assets for lower-frequency, niche details (e.g., 13 supplementary reference files in the 122B Deepening run for edge cases like cell-color extraction). General-to-specific organization recovered automatically from trajectory evidence. No vector index, no embedding store (in the default method). The merge itself is a hierarchical (tree) reduction over patches (L = ceil(log_{B_merge}|P|) levels, B_merge=32).
retriever_type: N/A for the proposed method at inference (no retriever; skill loaded directly). For the offline pipeline, an LLM acts as analyst/merge operator rather than a similarity retriever. The compared ReasoningBank-style baseline uses a dense retriever (Qwen3-Embedding-8B, top-1 memory), and the reproduced XSkill baseline uses lexical overlap top-3 (or Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), but these are baselines, not Trace2Skill.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (no learned retriever in Trace2Skill). Patch generation and consolidation are LLM-prompted (off-the-shelf frozen LLM as analyst/merge operator); selection of which patches to keep is by prevalence/coverage heuristics or, optionally, validation-pass-rate-guided Bayesian optimization (downstream-task-effectiveness signal), not a trained retrieval model. No contrastive/RL retriever training.
query_construction: N/A at inference (no query; the static skill is prepended to the agent context). Offline, the 'query' analog is each individual trajectory fed to an analyst: error trajectories go to an agentic error analyst that inspects artifacts, compares against ground truth, and validates a minimal fix; success trajectories go to a single-pass success analyst that extracts generalizable behavior patterns. Merge operator is given the initial skill S0 plus a batch of patches.
query_granularity: Offline analysis is trajectory-level (one patch proposed per trajectory). At inference there is no per-step or per-task query construction; the consolidated skill is loaded once and used throughout the episode.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot / never (test time): no retrieval is performed during inference; the evolved skill is loaded once at the start. Offline consolidation is itself a one-shot parallel batch process (not iterative online editing): all analysts run in a single parallel round, followed by ~2 hierarchical merge rounds (~3 sequential LLM-call rounds total).
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (no test-time retrieval trigger). The skill is always loaded (fixed schedule, prepended to context). Offline patch proposal is triggered per collected trajectory; the write/merge into the skill is triggered by the consolidation stage over the full patch pool.
reranking: No retrieval reranking. The closest analog is the merge operator M, which deduplicates patches, resolves conflicts, prefers prevalent/recurring patterns, and discards idiosyncratic edits during hierarchical consolidation (i.e., quality-prioritization of patches), plus deterministic diff-application guardrails (reject edits to missing files, withhold line-range conflicts, validate skill format). Optional Bayesian-optimization subset selection can be seen as a post-hoc patch reranking/selection but is not default.
retrieved_context_refinement: The consolidation IS the refinement: many trajectory-local patches are distilled, deduplicated, conflict-resolved, and merged into compact SoPs; idiosyncratic/low-support observations are routed to on-demand references/ files rather than the main SKILL.md (progressive disclosure). Failures that cannot be causally explained are excluded so the patch pool is grounded in verified failure mechanisms (distractor/noise filtering). No test-time context compression because there is no retrieval.
how_retrieved_used: Skill reuse via prompt augmentation: the consolidated SKILL.md is prepended/loaded into the agent's context at inference and used unchanged; auxiliary references/scripts are discovered procedurally on demand. No fine-tuning (theta is frozen), no latent-token injection, no test-time retrieval. The skill encodes reusable procedures (SoPs), guardrails, and tool-selection guidance that steer the ReAct agent's behavior.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan in the loose sense of load-skill-then-act: the static skill is provided up front and the frozen agent runs a ReAct (reason-act-observe) loop with bash/Python tools (up to 100 turns) using that fixed skill context for the whole episode. The skill itself encodes plan-time procedures (e.g., 'explore workbook structure before editing', 'run recalc.py after formula writes, then read back'). No MCTS/tree search and no per-step re-retrieval at inference. The offline pipeline (collect -> analyze -> merge) is a separate hierarchical consolidation, not in-loop planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-episode at inference (skill loaded once, fixed across the multi-turn ReAct rollout); no per-step/per-token/per-tool-call retrieval interleaving. Offline, analysis is per-trajectory and merging is hierarchical (multi-level reduction), but these are not interleaved with test-time reasoning.
retrieved_item_representation: Free-text / structured skill document: a human-readable SKILL.md of distilled procedural SoPs and guardrails (e.g., 'CRITICAL WARNING: run recalc.py after formula writes', 'prefer openpyxl over pandas.to_excel()', 'delete rows in descending order'), plus references/ files and deterministic scripts (e.g., recalc.py). Intermediate patches are diff-style JSON edits translated to unified diffs. Not raw trajectories, not latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled, reusable procedural skill / Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs). Many-to-one merging keeps operations that recur across trajectories and turns them into general principles rather than one-off, trajectory-specific tips; the paper frames consolidation as an INDUCTIVE generalization step over agent experience. Concretely, the 122B Deepening +Combined run's 323 patches coalesce into a few dominant SoPs (recalculation+read-back 55.1%, openpyxl-over-pandas 54.8%, explicit read-back verification 42.7%, structural-edit safety 16.4%).
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Agentic error analysis grounds patches in VERIFIED failure mechanisms: the error analyst inspects artifacts, compares against ground truth, and validates a minimal fix before proposing a patch; failures it cannot causally explain are excluded, reducing log-only false positives (parse-error mis-attribution drops from 57% for log-only LLM to 14% for the agentic analyst). (2) Prevalent-pattern bias in the merge operator: edits recurring across independent trajectories are kept as systematic SoPs while idiosyncratic edits are discarded. (3) Deterministic diff guardrails: reject edits to missing files, withhold line-range conflicts, validate skill format. (4) Niche/low-support observations routed to references/ instead of polluting SKILL.md. (5) A training-set validation step (selecting the best-of-3-seeds evolved skill that does not hurt training-set performance) guards against hallucinated harmful edits.
memory_type: procedural / skill-library (a static skill directory of SoPs). It is NOT an episodic test-time memory and NOT a retrieval index; the paper positions itself against experience-memory / retrieval-memory systems (Reflexion, Voyager, ReasoningBank, Memp, AWM, CER) by distilling many local observations into one static skill directory used without nearest-neighbor reuse.
write_back: Yes, but OFFLINE one-shot, not online: trajectories are analyzed into patches and the patches are consolidated and written once into the skill directory (replacing S0 with S*). There is no continuous write-back into a memory during deployment; after evolution the skill is frozen.
online_growth: No. The skill does not grow at test time; it is induced once offline from the evolving set and then frozen. The paper explicitly contrasts this with online/sequential editing and with test-time-growing retrieval memories. (Trajectory collection grows the trace pool, but only during the offline evolution stage.)
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure, offline batch (not per-step, not test-time). All evolving-set trajectories are labeled success/failure; +Error consolidates failures only, +Success consolidates successes only, +Combined consolidates both. Writing is a single consolidation event over the whole patch pool, applied via diff edits with deterministic guardrails, then optionally validated/selected on a held-out-from-test validation slice. Not human-validated per item (fully self-evolved) though qualitative SoP audits were done by the authors.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure, with an asymmetric design and a dedicated failure pathway. Failed trajectories drive an agentic error analyst (A-) that produces verified causal failure-cause items and corrective guardrails/SoPs (e.g., row-deletion safety, formula recalculation); successful trajectories drive a single-pass success analyst (A+) extracting reusable behavior patterns. +Error is often the most stable/transferable signal (e.g., strongest in math; cleanest cross-model transfer), and +Combined usually gives the largest Avg gain on spreadsheets and DocVQA. Failures that cannot be causally explained are dropped (grounded failure use, not log-only guesses).
memory_evolution_update: Refine-overwrite-by-consolidation (offline, one-shot): patches are deduplicated, conflict-resolved, and synthesized into general principles; the consolidated patch p* replaces/edits S0 to produce S*. Default applies ALL consolidated patches (no pruning). It is NOT append-only online editing; the paper shows parallel many-to-one consolidation beats order-dependent sequential editing (Seq-B=1 / Seq-B=4) in both quality (on most 122B metrics) and wall-clock (~3 min vs 15 min / 60 min). After evolution the skill is static (no further mutation).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. The default method has no learned/RL retrieval or selection policy; consolidation is LLM-prompted with prevalence/coverage heuristics. The optional patch-subset selectors (greedy top-1; Bayesian optimization with a TPE acquisition over binary inclusion vectors, validation-pass-rate objective) are search-based selection over patches, not a learned retrieval policy, and are non-default due to validation cost.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes - a central claim is cross-MODEL and cross-FAMILY portability of the learned skill artifact (not online memory sharing). Skills evolved from one model's traces transfer to other model scales (e.g., 35B-authored skill improves 122B), across families (Gemma-4-31B-it, GPT-5.5-high author and consume skills; Qwen->Gemma->GPT cross-model trace induction), and to OOD tasks. Because the artifact is a portable skill file, it can be loaded by heterogeneous agents/frameworks without parameter updates or retrieval. Headline: skills evolved from Qwen3.5-35B traces improve a Qwen3.5-122B agent by up to +57.65 pp on WikiTableQuestions.
benchmarks: Primary: SpreadsheetBench-Verified (400 samples split 200 evolve / 200 held-out test; also full SpreadsheetBench Soft/Hard on 2,529 examples with evolving-set removed). OOD table-QA transfer: WikiTableQuestions (2,810 examples, converted to spreadsheet tasks) and HiTab (1,585 examples). Math: DAPO-Math (400 evolve, 100 held-out test) and AIME 2026 (avg@8 over 30 problems, OOD). Vision/Doc QA: DocVQA (50 examples for evolution, 5,299 held-out test; ANLS and Acc=ANLS>=0.5). Broader document agents: PDF (VRDU Registration Forms -> VAREX Flat), PPTX (TSBench / Talk-to-Your-Slides, deck-disjoint OOD split), DOCX (generated tasks -> OfficeBench DOCX, 64 subtasks). Head-to-head appendix uses SpreadsheetBench-Verified 0:200/200:400 slices.
benchmark_family: Primarily tool / office-file-agent (SpreadsheetBench, OfficeBench DOCX, PPTX/TSBench, PDF/VRDU/VAREX) plus multi-hop/compositional table-QA (WikiTableQuestions, HiTab) as OOD, math reasoning (DAPO, AIME), and document VQA (DocVQA). Spans tool/code-style file manipulation, table QA, math, and multimodal doc-QA; no embodied or D4RL decision-RL benchmarks.
baselines: Skill baselines: No Skill (cli_only); Human-Written (Anthropic's official xlsx / pdf / docx / pptx skills); Parametric (LLM-generated skill from parametric knowledge alone). Trace2Skill variants: +Error, +Success, +Combined; Skill Deepening vs Skill Creation. Design-comparison baselines: sequential skill editing (Seq-B=1 update-after-every-trajectory, Seq-B=4 update-after-4); ReasoningBank-style retrieval memory (top-1 with Qwen3-Embedding-8B, success+failure lessons); single-call +Error LLM (log-only, no artifact inspection/validation); greedy top-1 and Bayesian-optimization patch selection; Anthropic skill-creator (Claude Code, Opus 4.6) external baseline. Head-to-head concurrent systems (Appendix G, shared Qwen3.5-122B): XSkill, EvoSkill (Claude Code and ReAct harnesses), SkillGen.
key_metrics: SpreadsheetBench: Vrf (verified instance pass rate), Soft (sub-problem pass rate), Hard (all-sub-problems-pass task pass rate); OOD table-QA pass rate (WikiTQ, HiTab). Summary metric Avg = (ID_avg + OOD_avg)/2, equally weighting in-distribution (SpreadsheetBench) and OOD across both user models. Math: DAPO-Test pass rate and AIME avg@8. DocVQA: ANLS and Accuracy (ANLS>=0.5, %). Broader doc agents: task-level pass rate (%). Efficiency: wall-clock skill-generation time (min). All spreadsheet results averaged over 3 seeds (41/42/43).
headline_result: Skills evolved from Qwen3.5-35B-A3B trajectories (Creation, +Error) improve a Qwen3.5-122B-A10B agent by up to +57.65 percentage points on WikiTableQuestions (OOD table-QA), demonstrating cross-scale, OOD transfer without parameter updates or test-time retrieval. On SpreadsheetBench-Verified Deepening, Human-Written+Combined reaches 69.83 Vrf (122B) vs 48.33 Human-Written and 27.67 No Skill. In the head-to-head (Appendix G, shared Qwen3.5-122B, held-out 200:400), Trace2Skill attains the highest Vrf (65.83 +Error, 69.83 +Combined), above XSkill (23.0), SkillGen (27.5), and EvoSkill (33.5 Claude Code / 59.5 ReAct), and the Human-Written 48.3 floor.
ablations: (1) Parallel vs sequential consolidation (same trace pool, +Error): Parallel beats Seq on most 122B SpreadsheetBench metrics (Vrf 65.83 vs 61.83 Seq-B=1 vs 59.00 Seq-B=4) and is far faster (~3 min vs 60 min Seq-B=1, 15 min Seq-B=4); Seq-B=1 is modestly higher only on 35B Soft/Hard. Math and DocVQA show parallel best-or-tied while fastest (math D-Test 95.0 vs 94.0/93.0; DocVQA Acc 92.52 vs 91.05/90.80). (2) Holistic skill vs ReasoningBank retrieval (same trajectory pool): +Combined beats ReasoningBank on Spreadsheet (122B Vrf 69.83 vs 56.00; 35B 29.67 vs 20.50), math (95.0 vs 94.0 D-Test), and DocVQA (Acc 92.52 vs 90.90). (3) Agentic vs single-call +Error LLM: agentic wins Avg in 3 of 4 author-mode blocks and most SpreadsheetBench columns; qualitative audit shows agentic identifies root causes more precisely (parse-error misattribution 14% vs 57%). (4) Analyst type: +Error vs +Success vs +Combined varies by domain (+Combined strongest on spreadsheet/DocVQA Avg; +Error most stable for math). (5) Selective patch aggregation: greedy top-1 plateaus below full aggregation (combinatorial patch value: side-effect flips, semantic overlap); BO selection improves +Error metrics (122B Deepening Vrf 65.83->69.83) but is validation-cost-heavy. (6) skill-creator (Opus 4.6) baseline does not improve over base on average; Trace2Skill +Error consistently stronger (Deepening avg 48.63 vs 23.33 vs 29.00 base).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Trace2Skill reports only end-to-end task metrics (Vrf/Soft/Hard, table-QA pass rate, DAPO/AIME, ANLS/Acc) plus efficiency (skill-generation wall-clock). It does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) because it is retrieval-free by design; the ReasoningBank baseline's retrieval is folded into its end-to-end scores. Patch-level analyses (coverage %, fail-to-pass/pass-to-fail flip counts, BO validation pass rate) are diagnostic but not standard intrinsic retrieval metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome-level (final task pass rate / ANLS). Some process-level diagnostics are reported: skill-generation wall-clock time (efficiency), per-SoP coverage shares among patches (e.g., 55.1%/54.8%/42.7%/16.4%), qualitative agentic-vs-LLM root-cause agreement (12.1% strong agreement, 54.5% disagreement on 33 audited cases; parse-error misattribution rates), and fail-to-pass/pass-to-fail flip analyses across greedy iterations. SpreadsheetBench Soft (sub-problem) is a partial-credit process-ish signal. No formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strongly emphasized for skill GENERATION cost: parallel consolidation produces a skill in ~3 min vs ~15 min (Seq-B=4, 5x slower) and ~60 min (Seq-B=1, 20x slower), with the gap scaling linearly in the number of traces N (~70 error lessons, W=128 workers, B_merge=32 => ~3 sequential LLM-call rounds: 1 analyst round + ~2 merge layers). Math: 2.0 min parallel vs 25.9 / 3.8 min sequential; DocVQA: 4.8 min vs 35.9 / 5.2 min. Inference cost is reduced relative to retrieval/online methods because the skill is loaded once with NO test-time retrieval, no parameter updates, and no growing memory. Total compute for all experiments/exploration ~20,000 A100 GPU-hours (8x A100 nodes). BO patch selection is flagged as the main extra-cost component (must materialize and score each candidate skill on a 32-task validation set).
context_budget_and_selection_count: The consolidated SKILL.md is kept compact and broadly-applicable (e.g., XSkill baseline's merged skill was ~865 words; Trace2Skill keeps the main doc focused while routing niche content to references/, used on demand). Default selection is FULL aggregation of all consolidated patches (no fixed-k cap); greedy/BO selection (BO keeps top m<=15 patches by coverage) are studied as alternatives. Merge batch size B_merge=32; Stage 2 runs 128 parallel sub-agents. Agent rollouts run up to 100 turns (max_turns=100); no separate tool-call budget imposed. Auxiliary files loaded on demand realize progressive disclosure rather than a fixed token budget.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses/adapts existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). Notable adaptations: SpreadsheetBench-Verified 400 split 200/200; full SpreadsheetBench Soft/Hard on 2,529 examples (evolving-set removed); WikiTableQuestions (2,810) and HiTab (1,585) converted into spreadsheet-format OOD tasks; DAPO-Math 400 evolve/100 test; AIME 2026 (30 problems, avg@8); DocVQA 50 evolve/5,299 test; PDF VRDU Registration Forms->VAREX Flat; PPTX TSBench deck-disjoint OOD; DOCX generated tasks->64 OfficeBench DOCX subtasks (max_turns=100). All scored by each benchmark's official/local verifier.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: no (no test-time case retrieval; offline it 'retrieves'/collects trajectories but not for nearest-neighbor reuse), Reuse: yes (the consolidated skill/SoPs are reused at inference, loaded directly), Revise: yes (offline patch proposal + agentic fix-validation + hierarchical merge revise the skill; the error analyst writes and re-evaluates a minimal fix), Retain: yes (consolidated patches are written/retained once into the static skill directory)]. It realizes Reuse/Revise/Retain offline but deliberately omits test-time Retrieve, which is its key contrast with CBR/retrieval-memory systems.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames the consolidation as INDUCTIVE reasoning over agent experience (citing inductive-reasoning works) and positions itself within 'agent skills' and 'experience memory for agent self-evolution' literatures. It realizes CBR-like Reuse/Revise/Retain mechanisms under a skill-evolution framing.
tool_document_engineering: Partially applicable: the learned skill is essentially engineered TOOL/PROCEDURE documentation distilled from execution traces. Skill writing follows Anthropic skill-creator guidance; recurring lessons become concise actionable SoPs with explicit tool-selection guidance (e.g., 'use openpyxl for write-back, not pandas.to_excel(); copy input file first'), deterministic helper scripts (recalc.py), and a general-to-specific layout (SKILL.md for universal rules, references/ for edge cases). Not embedding-based tool-doc augmentation; it is LLM-induced procedural documentation grounded in trajectories.
index_content_separation: Yes (progressive disclosure / on-demand references). The root SKILL.md holds broadly-reusable procedures while low-support/niche details are routed to references/ files loaded on demand (e.g., 13 supplementary reference files in the 122B Deepening run). The agent still procedurally discovers referenced resources/scripts that are not preloaded, mirroring standard skill-loading lightweight-index-then-content practice; Trace2Skill recovers this hierarchy automatically from trajectory evidence.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no live tool registry / MCP / RapidAPI / RESTful index). The agent uses a ReAct harness with bash + Python (command-line tools, openpyxl, etc.) over local files; the skill is a static directory, not a synchronized external tool index.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency graph). The learned SoPs do encode procedural ordering/safety constraints (e.g., run recalc.py after formula writes then read back; delete rows in descending order to avoid index-shift corruption; copy input workbook before editing), which are workflow prerequisites rather than a modeled tool-dependency retrieval graph.
adaptation_mechanism: Execution-feedback-driven, agentic revision plus LLM-prompted inductive generalization. The error analyst (A-) runs a ReAct loop that inspects artifacts, compares to ground truth, and validates a minimal fix before proposing a patch (execution-feedback-driven revision); the success analyst (A+) does single-pass pattern abstraction; the merge operator M performs inductive generalization (prefer prevalent patterns, discard idiosyncratic). The adapted artifact (skill) is then reused verbatim at inference (no per-case test-time adaptation, no RL reuse-finetuning).
builds_on: Agent-skills framing (Anthropic skills; skill-creator guidance; official xlsx/pdf/docx/pptx document skills); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) harness; experience-memory / self-evolution line (Reflexion, Voyager, ReasoningBank [Ouyang et al. 2026], Memp, AWM/Agent Workflow Memory, Contextual Experience Replay, Investigate-Consolidate-Exploit, skill-set optimization); inductive-reasoning-with-LLMs works; serving via vLLM; uses Qwen3.5-122B-A10B / Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (instruct+thinking hybrid MoE), Gemma-4-31B-it, GPT-5.5-high; Qwen3-Embedding for baseline retrieval. Benchmarks: SpreadsheetBench, WikiTableQuestions, HiTab, DAPO, AIME 2026, DocVQA, VRDU/VAREX, TSBench/Talk-to-Your-Slides, OfficeBench.
contrasts_with: (1) Online/sequential skill editing (order-dependent updates after each trace) - Trace2Skill does parallel many-to-one consolidation (faster, generally stronger, order-independent). (2) Experience/retrieval memories queried at test time, especially ReasoningBank (also Reflexion, Voyager, Memp, AWM, CER) - Trace2Skill distills into one static skill used without test-time retrieval. (3) Log-only single-call error analysis - Trace2Skill uses agentic artifact-inspecting, fix-validating error analysis. (4) Skill-augmented RL / intrinsic skill evolution / meta-learning that update a policy or maintain test-time memory - Trace2Skill keeps theta frozen and produces a portable artifact. (5) Concurrent skill-evolution systems XSkill, EvoSkill, SkillGen (head-to-head, Trace2Skill higher Vrf) and Anthropic skill-creator (Opus 4.6, no average improvement).
lineage: Group F (decision/experience memory & RL-adjacent self-evolving agents) and the agent-skill / experience-memory lineage. A 2026 'trajectory-to-skill' method that advances the Reflexion -> Voyager -> AWM -> ReasoningBank experience-memory line by replacing test-time retrieval/online editing with offline, parallel, inductive consolidation of broad trajectories into one portable, retrieval-free static skill directory. Distinctive contributions: (a) many-to-one parallel consolidation as inductive generalization (vs order-dependent sequential edits), (b) a single distilled skill beating ReasoningBank-style episodic retrieval, (c) agentic (artifact-inspecting, fix-validating) error analysis, and (d) demonstrated cross-scale, cross-family, and OOD portability of the learned skill artifact without parameter updates or retrieval.
